newsitem.title: USA: Calif. gunman kills policeman, is found dead.
newsitem.headline: Calif. gunman kills policeman, is found dead.

text.p: A gunman holed up in a warehouse shot and killed a policeman in a hail of bullets and wounded two other officers who rushed to their stricken colleague's aid, authorities said Wednesday.
The gunman, who held police at bay for several hours after the killing late Tuesday night, was found dead when a Special Weapons and Tactics team stormed the building early Wednesday.
Interim Los Angeles Police Chief Bayan Lewis said it was not known if the man was killed by police gunfire or shot himself. "There was a lot of gunfire exchanged," he said.

The dead officer, Det. Charles Lazzaretto, 30, and a colleague, both members of the suburban Glendale police force, entered the warehouse just before midnight to search for the suspect, who was wanted for questioning in a domestic violence episode, Glendale Police Sgt. Rick Young said.
Lazzaretto was immediately cut down by bullets from a semi-automatic rifle, Young said, and his colleague was pinned down by gunfire and unable to go to his aid.

Young said two Los Angeles police officers who responded to an "officer down" call were also met by a hail of bullets. Officer Jude Bella, 24, was hit five times and Kevin Foster, 26, was also hit, but the injuries were not life-threatening.
Officers tried throughout the night to enter the warehouse to arrest the gunman but each time they were driven back by gunfire, Lewis said.

Police tossed flash grenades into the building at one point to divert the gunman's attention and managed to storm in and rescue the trapped Glendale officer but they were unable to get to Lazzaretto, who was further inside the warehouse.
Lazzaretto, the father of two sons aged three and five, was a 10-year veteran. He was the fourth Glendale officer to die in the line of duty in the history of the force.
